name: nlgeom-uniaxial-svk
reference: Benchmark K1. The only Command-level case with an *exact* finite-strain answer, and the reason it is exact is that the linear elastic law evaluated on Green-Lagrange strain and second Piola-Kirchhoff stress IS the St Venant-Kirchhoff material. A 1 m bar of a nu = 0 material is stretched 10 % by a prescribed displacement against three symmetry planes. With nu = 0 the Lame constant is zero, so a traction-free lateral face means E22 = E33 = 0 and the exact deformation is F = diag(1.1, 1, 1) everywhere: E11 = (lambda^2 - 1)/2 = 0.105, S11 = E * 0.105 = 22050 MPa, the first Piola-Kirchhoff stress is lambda S11 = 24255 MPa and the Cauchy stress is F S F^T / det F = lambda S11 = 24255 MPa as well, because the cross-section does not change. The root reaction is the first Piola-Kirchhoff stress on the reference area, 24255 MPa x 0.01 m^2 = 242.55 MN. Every number here is closed form; the tolerance is 1e-9 relative, which is round-off. A small-strain formulation would answer 0.1 for E11 and 21000 MPa for the stress, 5 % and 13 % away, so this also separates the two formulations outright.
